text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bar-On Affair decision today; Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu unlikely to be indicted.
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat orders renewal of security cooperation with Israel.
- Kiryat Bialik man dies of heart attack while trying to kill wife.

- Serious report on Bar-On affair will be published this evening but an indictment will be issued apparently only against Aryeh Deri. Conclusion: Interested elements and criminal suspects tried to take over state prosecution.
- Israeli army chief denies rumours missing airman Ron Arad rescued in military action.
- In Haaretz tomorrow: South Africa confirms Israel helped it develop nuclear weapons.
- Army chief Amnon Shahak and Shin Bet chief Ami Ayalon met Yasser Arafat in Gaza on Thursday night.
- Committee: Education Ministry security chief responsible for foul-up at Naharayim in Jordan where seven girls killed.
- Netanyahu: Under no circumstances do I intend to quit.
- Foreign investors announce delays in their coming to Israel until the political situation is clarified.
- Netanyahu: There's a difference between a mistake in judgment and a criminal act.
